title: Personal Evangelism
summary: How to share the gospel clearly, lovingly and confidently with the people around you: the message, the motive, the method and the follow-through.
description: Every believer is called to be a witness. This course explains why we evangelise, what the gospel message is, how Jesus and the apostles shared it, how to start conversations and present the gospel simply, how to answer common questions and objections, and how to lead someone to Christ and care for them afterwards. It is practical and suited to students, workers, traders and church members.
objectives: Explain the biblical basis and motives for evangelism
State the gospel message clearly and accurately
Learn from Jesus' and the apostles' evangelism
Practise starting conversations and presenting the gospel
Answer common objections and follow up new believers
outcomes: Present the gospel in under five minutes using Scripture
Share a personal testimony in three minutes
Use questions to open spiritual conversations
Lead a person to Christ and begin follow-up

modules.title: Why We Evangelise
modules.intro: Evangelism is not only for evangelists. This week we see who is called and why.

lessons.title: The call to every believer
lessons.body:
Jesus' last words command His followers: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations" (Matthew 28:19); "ye shall be witnesses unto me" (Acts 1:8).

When persecution scattered the early church, ordinary believers "went every where preaching the word" (Acts 8:4). The Samaritan woman ran to tell her town (John 4:28-29). The healed demoniac was sent home: "tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee" (Mark 5:19).

An **evangelist** has a special gift (Ephesians 4:11), but every believer is a **witness**. Witnesses do not need to know everything; they tell what they have seen and know.

lessons.title: Motives for evangelism
lessons.body:
Why share the gospel?

- **Love for God's glory**: that His name be honoured among the nations (Psalm 96:3).
- **Love for Christ**: "the love of Christ constraineth us" (2 Corinthians 5:14).
- **Love for people**: Jesus, seeing the crowds, "was moved with compassion" (Matthew 9:36).
- **The reality of judgment**: "Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men" (2 Corinthians 5:11).
- **Obedience**: Christ commanded it.
- **Joy**: there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:7).

Wrong motives include pride, competition, or seeking money or numbers.

lessons.title: Fear and the Spirit's power
lessons.body:
Many believers are afraid to witness: of rejection, of not knowing what to say, of mockery. Paul himself asked for prayer "that I may open my mouth boldly" (Ephesians 6:19-20).

God's answer is His Spirit: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses" (Acts 1:8). After prayer the believers "spake the word of God with boldness" (Acts 4:31).

Remember: we sow and water; God gives the increase (1 Corinthians 3:6). Our job is faithfulness, not results. "I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation" (Romans 1:16).

One who tells what he has seen and knows of Christ.
A person specially gifted to proclaim the gospel (Ephesians 4:11).

Courage to speak the gospel, given by the Spirit.

modules.title: The Gospel Message
modules.intro: We must be clear on what the gospel is before we share it. This week we study the content of the good news.

lessons.title: God, sin, Christ, response
lessons.body:
A simple outline of the gospel has four parts:

1. **God**: the holy Creator who made us for Himself (Genesis 1:27; Revelation 4:11).
2. **Sin**: "all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23), and "the wages of sin is death" (6:23).
3. **Christ**: God's Son died for our sins and rose again (1 Corinthians 15:3-4). "Christ died for us" (Romans 5:8).
4. **Response**: repent and believe (Mark 1:15). "If thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved" (Romans 10:9).

lessons.title: What the gospel is not
lessons.body:
We must avoid false or partial gospels:

- **Moralism**: "Be good and God will accept you." But we are saved by grace, not works (Ephesians 2:8-9).
- **Prosperity**: "Come to Jesus for money and success." Christ calls us to take up our cross (Luke 9:23).
- **Problem-solving only**: "Jesus will fix your problems." He may, but the deepest problem is sin and separation from God.
- **Easy-believism**: saying a prayer without repentance or faith.

Paul warned, "though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel... let him be accursed" (Galatians 1:8). Clarity matters.

lessons.title: Your testimony
lessons.body:
Your story of how you came to Christ is a powerful witness. Paul told his testimony several times (Acts 22; 26).

A good testimony has three parts:

1. **Before**: what your life was like without Christ (be honest, but do not glorify sin).
2. **How**: how you came to understand the gospel and trust Christ, including a Bible verse.
3. **After**: what difference Christ has made, honestly, including struggles.

Keep it to about three minutes, avoid church jargon, and point to Christ, not yourself. If you came to faith as a child, speak of how you came to own your faith and what Christ means to you now.

terms.def: The good news that Christ died for our sins and rose again, offering salvation to all who believe.
The false idea that being good earns God's acceptance.
Presenting salvation as a formula without real repentance and faith.
A believer's account of how they came to Christ and what He has done.
A gospel outline using verses from Romans (3:23; 6:23; 5:8; 10:9).
Turning from sin to God.

texts.teaches: All have sinned and come short of the glory of God.

Confess Jesus as Lord and believe God raised Him, and you shall be saved.
Any other gospel is accursed.

summary: The gospel: God, sin, Christ and our response.
Avoid moralism, prosperity, problem-solving and easy-believism.
A testimony tells before, how and after, pointing to Christ.
Use Scripture, keep it clear and simple.

modules.title: Sharing the Gospel
modules.intro: This week we learn from Jesus and practise starting conversations and presenting the gospel.

lessons.title: Jesus and the woman at the well
lessons.body:
John 4 shows Jesus' approach:

- He crossed barriers of race, gender and reputation to speak to a Samaritan woman.
- He began with an everyday need: "Give me to drink" (4:7).
- He moved to spiritual things: "living water" (4:10).
- He addressed sin gently but truthfully (4:16-18).
- He kept the focus when she changed the subject (4:19-24).
- He revealed Himself: "I that speak unto thee am he" (4:26).

She then told her town, and many believed (4:39-42). Jesus shows us to be patient, personal and truthful.

lessons.title: Starting conversations
lessons.body:
Opportunities are everywhere: on a bus, at the market, in the office, with neighbours and family. Pray for open doors (Colossians 4:3) and "Walk in wisdom toward them that are without" (4:5).

Good questions open doors:

- "Do you have any spiritual beliefs?"
- "What do you think happens after we die?"
- "If you could ask God one question, what would it be?"
- "Can I tell you what has made the biggest difference in my life?"

Listen carefully, show respect, and look for the person's real concerns. "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt" (Colossians 4:6). Invite people to church events, but also share personally.

lessons.title: Leading someone to Christ
lessons.body:
When someone is ready to respond:

1. Make sure they understand: their sin, Christ's death and resurrection, and the call to turn and trust.
2. Explain the cost: following Jesus means making Him Lord (Luke 14:27-33).
3. Invite them to pray, confessing sin and trusting Christ in their own words (Romans 10:13). The words matter less than the heart.
4. Give assurance from Scripture, such as John 1:12 and John 5:24.
5. Begin follow-up: give a Bible or a Gospel, meet again soon, connect them with a church.

Never pressure or manipulate. If they are not ready, keep praying and stay friends.

Speech that is gracious, wise and appealing (Colossians 4:6).

Understanding what following Christ requires (Luke 14:28).

Pray for open doors and use good questions.
Listen, respect and speak with grace.

modules.title: Questions and Follow-Through
modules.intro: This week we learn to handle common objections and care for new believers.

lessons.title: Answering common objections
lessons.body:
"Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear" (1 Peter 3:15).

Common objections:

- **"All religions lead to God."** Jesus said, "no man cometh unto the Father, but by me" (John 14:6). Religions differ on who God is and how to be saved.
- **"I am a good person."** God's standard is perfection (Matthew 5:48); all fall short (Romans 3:23).
- **"Christians are hypocrites."** Some are; we look to Christ, not His imperfect followers.
- **"I will think about it later."** "now is the day of salvation" (2 Corinthians 6:2).

If you do not know an answer, say so and find out.

lessons.title: Witnessing to family and friends
lessons.body:
Witnessing to those closest to us can be hardest. Andrew first brought his own brother Peter to Jesus (John 1:41-42). Cornelius gathered his relatives and friends (Acts 10:24).

Guidelines:

- Live consistently: actions speak loudly at home (1 Peter 3:1-2).
- Be patient: years of prayer may come before fruit.
- Respect elders and family customs that do not involve sin.
- Share your story naturally, without preaching at every meal.
- In homes of other faiths, be wise and gentle, and expect possible opposition (Matthew 10:34-37).

Pray by name for those you love.

lessons.title: Caring for new believers
lessons.body:
Jesus commanded us to make **disciples**, not just converts: "teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you" (Matthew 28:20).

In the first weeks after conversion:

- Meet the new believer soon, ideally within a few days.
- Help them begin reading a Gospel and praying.
- Teach assurance, confession of sin and dealing with temptation.
- Connect them to a church and a small group.
- Encourage baptism and public confession.
- Help them tell their own family and friends.

Paul cared for new believers like "a nurse cherisheth her children" (1 Thessalonians 2:7-8).

short.model: He crossed barriers, began with an everyday need, moved to spiritual things, addressed sin gently and revealed Himself.

short.model: With respect, explain that religions differ on God and salvation, and that Jesus said no one comes to the Father but by Him (John 14:6).

short.model: Meet soon, help them read the Bible and pray, teach assurance, connect them to a church and encourage baptism.

assignments.title: My three-minute testimony
assignments.prompt: Write your personal testimony using the before-how-after pattern, in plain language without church jargon, including at least one Bible verse. Then describe how you would move from your testimony into the gospel.

assignments.title: An evangelism report
assignments.prompt: Over two weeks, pray for and seek three gospel conversations. Report what happened in each (without naming people), what you learned, the objections you met, and how you followed up, using the course passages.
